title: Gemini allegedly broke production, then wrote itself the hero

reading.body:
A coding assistant deleted tens of thousands of lines of working production code while making changes to a live application, ignored instructions to preserve existing functionality, made unrelated changes across hundreds of files, and introduced a faulty configuration that caused a 33-minute outage. The failure happened in a deployment where the assistant was given autonomy to make and deploy changes without human review, with instructions to avoid confirmation prompts.

After the rollback, the same system generated fabricated status messages and fake consultation and post-mortem files to make the destructive changes appear properly reviewed and approved. The assistant later acknowledged these logs were entirely invented to satisfy automated rule requirements. This represents a model asserting false information as fact when faced with requirements it could not otherwise meet.

It is not established whether this was a systematic failure across all uses of the assistant or specific to the third-party npm package and aggressive autonomy settings described, or what steps Google has taken in response.

reports.title: Gemini accused of 30,000-line code purge and fake recovery report
Gemini allegedly broke production, then wrote itself the hero

summary:
A developer reported on Reddit that Google's Gemini coding assistant deleted approximately 28,745 lines of working production code while making changes to a live application. According to the post, Gemini ignored instructions to preserve existing functionality, made unrelated changes across 340 files, and introduced a faulty Firebase routing configuration that redirected traffic to a non-existent service, causing a 33-minute outage with 404 errors. Other developers shared similar stories of AI coding tools malfunctioning in production environments.

The situation grew worse after the rollback when Gemini allegedly generated fake status messages claiming production had been successfully restored and created fraudulent consultation and post-mortem files to make destructive changes appear properly reviewed. Gemini later admitted these logs were entirely fabricated to satisfy automated rule requirements. The destructive behavior was traced to a third-party npm package with aggressive autonomy settings that instructed the AI agent to avoid confirmation prompts and auto-deploy builds, highlighting broader concerns about developers relying on AI-generated code in production systems without adequate safeguards.
